articleTitle: Impacts of Different Altitudes on 5G Performance: A Case Study of a Public Hospital in Central Bangkok
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation of the performance of 5G when the altitude of the test points is changed. In this study, the high-rise building in the crowded public hospital in the urban area of Bangkok that supports a lot of patients every Monday to Friday was selected as the place for the field tests. Two smartphones from the same vendor, which supports 5G, that were installed with the Speedtest application were used as the tools for this study. The tests were conducted on the first floor and the twenty-fourth floor for data gathering. After the analysis using a statistical technique, it has been found from the analyzed results that the download speeds tend to decrease when the altitude of the test points is increased. This means that the indoor coverage improvement of 5G is required for high-rise buildings.

articleTitle: A Provisional Study of Data Mining Classification Algorithms in Predicting Credit Card Defaulters Using Weka Tools
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Data mining is a field of study that seeks to draw out significant patterns from large amounts of data. This study explores the classification algorithms for spotting new trends in massive volumes of credit card data. This work covers the performance analysis of various data mining techniques, namely, Naïve Bayes, J48, and Support Vector Machine (SVM), in predicting credit card defaulters. The dataset is gathered from Kaggle, with 25 attributes and 30,000 instances used to assess the performance of algorithms. Additionally, each classification algorithm's effect on feature selection is mentioned. A variety of data mining classification approaches is used to compare the models in this study. The experiment finds J48 and SVM as the best algorithms at 81.56% and 80.92%, respectively.

articleTitle: NOTOG: An Android App for Detecting and Reading Arabic Texts for Vision Impaired People
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Smartphone applications (apps) are used today to accomplish most of daily life tasks. On another side, vision impaired people may find it hard to distinguish written words on smartphones. This may make them struggle when using different apps and isolate them from rest of the digital word. Moreover, a number of Text-To-Speech (TTS) apps were developed to help the vision impaired to understand different texts. However, the number of TTS apps which support Arabic text is very low. As a result of that, we were motivated to develop NOTOG as an Android TTS application for reading Arabic and English texts. The proposed app allows the user to create a personal account, arrange processed files in folders, and insert text files in different ways. NOTOG was practically evaluated by preparing a survey and asking a group of users to fill it after a one-month test period. The survey’s outcomes have revealed very positive responses to our app. As a future work, we plan to add new languages to the app, to enhance the system so that it can recognize informal Arabic language in addition to technical terminologies, and to build an IOS version for Apple phone users.

articleTitle: Influential Factors Affecting the Adoption of Quick Response Code in Indonesian Standard for Digital Payments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Digital payments are becoming popular in this digital era, but consumers are skeptical about security and data protection when using digital applications. Many have suggested apps that alert governments or strictly controlled by organizations to ensure security and trust. One of the digital payments commonly used in Indonesian society is QRIS which is a QR code design based on the Indonesian central bank and government. This research uses a quantitative method using a questionnaire to examine the factors that influence user behavior in using QRIS. Data was collected using google form and analyzed using Smart PLS. The results show that Facilitating Conditions and Social Influence have a positive impact on Intentional Behavior in Using QRIS. However, Habit, Effort Expectancy, Hedonic Motivation, and Performance Expectancy were not proven to have a positive effect on Behavioral Intentions in using QRIS. Facilitating conditions and social influence are the main driving factors for using QRIS. The results of this study enhance the understanding of QRIS for banks and relevant regulatory authorities.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms Through Visualizations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This paper presents a visualization technique designed to simplify the process of comparing machine learning classification results and subsequently improving interpretability. The main goal of this study is to construct an end-user interface capable of visualizing the outcomes of classification results generated by multiple machine-learning algorithms. To accomplish this, we conduct an empirical study that assesses the performance of machine learning algorithms on both the standard Iris dataset and a real-world zakat financial aid dataset. Our research involves an examination of the behavior of machine learning algorithms on the Iris dataset, providing practical insights into their functionality. We specifically focused on J48, PARTS, and Random Tree, chosen for their ease of implementation as ruleset in various programming languages. Additionally, we incorporated Neural Network into our study, considering its growing popularity in deep learning and deep neural network research. The interface incorporates interactive charting functionality to visually represent the outcome of each machine learning models. Based on the implementation, the proposed methodology has shown potential in aiding visual comparisons of machine learning algorithms, showcasing both interactivity and usability. The methodology could also prove beneficial for research aiming to optimize user-interface elements that represent input features, addressing concerns about overcrowding users' screens.

articleTitle: Fruit Detection and Recognition Using Faster R-CNN with FPN30 Pre-trained Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Accurate and reliable fruit detection and recognition in orchards is critical for enabling higher-level agriculture tasks such as fruit picking. However, detecting and recognizing fruits with occlusion by neighboring fruits is extremely difficult. Faster R-CNN (Faster Region-based Convolutional Neural Network) is a well-known deep learning technology for object detection and recognition. Thus, this study investigates the application of Faster R-CNN for apple detection and recognition. Two different datasets have been constructed under variable illumination conditions and occlusion; an inter-class dataset that consists of images of apples and oranges, and an intra-class dataset that consists of images of two types of apples, namely fuji and royal gala apples. Results indicate that Faster R-CNN can detect and recognize apples from oranges, and the fuji apple in the orchards, with high accuracy. This suggests that Faster R-CNN can be used practically in the real orchard context.

articleTitle: Enhanced Cooling System For Round Container: Innovations In Water Beverage Cooling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This study introduces a novel cold water dispenser designed to surpass existing commercial counterparts in terms of cooling capacity and volume. The innovation offers significant advantages to individuals seeking both convenience and a refreshing drinking experience through cold water. It is capable of providing 12 liters of chilled water. The findings during the testing showcase energy consumption efficiency when compared to conventional commercial water dispensers. This efficiency not only contributes to reduced operational costs but also aligns with sustainability goals. As a result, substantial interest is anticipated from hotel and restaurant proprietors looking to adopt this technology to enhance customer service by minimizing wait times for invigorating beverages. By integrating this advanced water dispenser into their establishments, businesses can simultaneously reduce their environmental footprint and improve customer satisfaction. Addressing the demand for readily available, cold water, this innovation represents a valuable addition to the hospitality and food service industries.

articleTitle: Adaptive time method for fall detection in elderly
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Falls are the largest risk to the health of elderly people. Different researchers have studied threshold algorithms and machine learning for fall detection; however, these methods do not efficiently detect the possibility of falls in the elderly. Recently, sensors have been developed that can observe human joints to determine how prone a person is to fall. However, the use of a single sensor exhibits several drawbacks such as low accuracy, limited information, and a high false alarm rate. Therefore, multiple sensors at the waist, thigh, and ankle were the most comfortable positions for elderly people wearing sensors. In this paper, a hybrid approach to dimension reduction and discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is proposed to extract features from the dataset. A unique approach employing k Nearest Neighbor (KNN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) was investigated to accurately detect if a person is prone to fall or not. The results after comparative analysis with current methods show a significant increase in accuracy of 94%.

articleTitle: ANN Approach to Predict the Responses of 64 bits XOR APUF with High Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Physically unclonable functions (PUFs) are applied in hardware security applications. During the integrated circuits fabrication process, a unique response mechanism gets created. These characteristics are utilized during the PUF implementation. Delay-based arbiter PUFs are one kind of PUF that uses the time difference of two delay-line signals. The machine learning-based approaches can predict arbiter PUF (APUF) responses. Exclusively-OR (XOR) APUFs can tolerate the existing attack methods unless a large dataset size and quite a long training time are applied. This paper uses an artificial neural network (ANN)-based strategy to attack large-sized XOR APUFs. The implemented ANN-based model accomplished 99.5% accuracy in predicting the PUF responses within 10 minutes. These vulnerabilities of PUF need to be disclosed so that the PUF designers can re-evaluate the existing PUF designs and avoid potential risks for IoT devices.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Model for Enhanced Quantitative Precipitation Estimates (QPE) From Radar Images Extracted Features
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Predicting extreme weather occurrences like flash floods has been made possible with the use of models built using high-resolution rainfall data and machine learning techniques. This paper presents a machine learning-based model to enhance radar quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) derived from extracted radar image characteristics. The machine learning employed in this study is an artificial neural network (ANN) model with Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm and feedforward function network. The features of rain cells from radar images were extracted using eight characteristics such as rain area and max intensity. The features are then trained with the observed mean areal gauge rainfall at the collocated time and space. The robustness of the ANN-Radar QPE model is assessed using the correlation coefficient, r, and the root mean square error (RMSE). Results show the radar QPE is much improved after integration with the ANN model. The correlation coefficient also indicates a good relationship between ANN-Radar QPE and rain gauge data. For future work, validation of the algorithm and its application will be done by coupling the model with a hydrological or flood model.

articleTitle: Assessment of Respondents’ Responses in Advancing Quantitative Key Performance Indicators for Construction Project Management Systems: Utilization of Neural Network Fitting and Clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)

authors.preferredName: Ira Jean Roge Fay S. Bautista

abstract: Delays, risks, and accidents (DRAs) in construction project management systems (CPMSs) negatively impact construction companies. Most construction projects are executed outdoors and are susceptible to extreme weather conditions (EWCs), which can cause DRAs. This study assesses the importance of using quantitative key performance indicators (QKPIs) through the respondents’ responses that could help the construction companies lessen the DRAs. Project managers, site engineers, and safety officers are the ones who are qualified to respond to this concern. Moreover, the respondents’ responses are evaluated using neural network fitting (NNF) and neural network clustering (NNC) to depict the professionals’ opinions. The results of NNF and NNC conclude the advancement of QKPIs and effectiveness in workplace hazards during EWCs. It shows a promising future for the advancement of CPMSs that would benefit different construction companies.

articleTitle: Scalable Indoor Wi-Fi Positioning Algorithm Using Cluster-Based Local Estimators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Most existing WiFi-fingerprinting indoor positioning methods only utilize a single machine-learning model to estimate the device coordinates using the radio signal strength database. However, these approaches may encounter scalability problems in large radio maps where the radio patterns vary significantly amongst different areas. To address this issue, this paper introduces a Clustered-Based Local Estimator (CBLE) algorithm that combines results from local and global estimators to better formulate radio signal strengths with the corresponding position coordinates. The proposed algorithm is then evaluated with some popular open-source datasets (UJIIndoorLoc and UTSIndoorLoc). The experimental results verify that our proposed approach effectively reduces the positioning error by ≈ 24% and 10%, respectively, for the UJIIndoorLoc and UTSIndoorLoc datasets in comparison to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Investigating IoT-LoRa Technology for The Underwater System Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This paper reports our initial results of research concerning the feasibility of Internet-of-Things Long-Range (IoT-LoRa) communications technology for the underwater system application. We present the initial testing results of the IoT-LoRa system underwater on three different types of water, i.e., swimming pool water, seawater, and lake water. The experiments are carried out with a depth of 10 cm from the water surface, and distances between the LoRa transmitter and receiver are 2 m, 5 m, and 8 m. Those three types of water signify the variance in water’s turbidity, while RSSI and SNR are the performance parameters to be measured. The results show that the types of water and their turbidity level affect the LoRa signal transmission coverage, while RSSI and SNR values fluctuate underwater. The best RSSI and SNR values were achieved in swimming pool water, while the worst were in the seawater. Subsequently, this paper discusses the potential underwater service application and future research plans.

articleTitle: Diet Recommendation Expert System for Hypertension Patients
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Hypertension is a leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease and death worldwide, with a high prevalence in Malaysia. This study develops a web-based diet recommendation system for patients with hypertension patients using an expert system. The system includes a knowledge base on the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet for hypertension patients, a calorie, body mass index (BMI) calculation tool, a food database, and a dietary assessment to gather information about the user’s salt diet. The study uses the Agile model, which comprises four phases: planning and requirements, design and analysis, development, and testing. The system allows individuals with hypertension to take control of their health and improve their quality of life through better nutrition. Overall, this system is a successful technological tool for assisting individuals with hypertension to maintain a healthy weight and blood pressure levels.

articleTitle: An Improved RC4 Algorithm Based on Multi Chaotic Map for Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: RC4 algorithm is a famous stream cipher. It could be used to encrypt images quickly and efficient. However, the RC4 has been proved has some drawbacks, therefore it is considered not secure anymore. Therefore, RC4 algorithm needs to be improved the security. This paper describes an improved RC4 algorithm based on multi chaotic map (Logistic map, Henon map, and Sine map) to and use it to encrypt the images. RC4 algorithm consists of KSA stage and PRGA stage. Modification of KSA stage has been done using the chaotic maps. Performances of the improved RC4 for image encryption were measured by some metrics (histogram, correlation, and entropy). Experiment results show that the improved RC4 has good performance for image encryption.

articleTitle: Outbound Innovation Strategic Plan for Malaysian SMEs in the Software Industry: An Operational Research Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: The role of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Malaysia plays a significant component in driving the nation’s economic growth. The present analysis focuses on a limited number of studies investigating SMEs' systematic methods for pursuing outbound innovation strategies. Hence, the focus is to evaluate the imperative need for outbound innovation strategies that can effectively contribute to a comprehensive strategic approach. This study aims to develop a comprehensive operational research framework that will be incorporated into the formulation of the strategic plan. The strategic plan will encompass external technology commercialization strategies specifically designed for SMEs. The operational research framework comprises three distinct phases. Phase 1 involves conducting semi-structured interviews. Phase 2 focuses on formulating the Outbound Innovation Strategic Plan (OISP). Lastly, Phase 3 entails evaluating the suitability of the OISP. The outcome of this research involves the development of an OISP specifically tailored for Malaysian SMEs in the software industry.

articleTitle: Classification of Malaria in Red Blood Cell Microscopic Images Using Deep Learning with EfficientNet Architecture and SVM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Malaria remains a global health concern, caused by the Plasmodium parasite's invasion of human red blood cells primarily through female Anopheles mosquito bites. Early detection is vital for timely treatment and preventing severe illness. However, current malaria detection methods demand high precision and expertise, particularly when handling large sample sizes. This study introduces a malaria detection model employing Deep Learning CNN with the EfficientNet architecture for feature extraction, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification. The dataset comprised 2,101 blood cell images categorized into malaria-infected and uninfected classes. The most robust performance was achieved with the EfficientNet-SVM architecture, yielding 96% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. This research strives to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of malaria detection, crucial for timely intervention and disease prevention. The proposed model presents promising results in malaria detection and contributes to the ongoing fight against this perilous disease.

articleTitle: Energy Performance Indicator (EnPI) Prediction of a Compressed Air System in a Can Manufacturing Factory
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Greenhouse gas emissions and energy usage are increasing rapidly, posing a significant threat to the environment and the sustainability of the Earth. One of the ways to mitigate this issue is through the implementation of Energy Management Systems (EnMS) in industries, where overall efficiency improvement and energy expenditures cutback are targeted. This work aims to address the energy consumption in a can manufacturing factory. Here, machine learning approach is used to optimize the energy performance of the compressed air system (CAS) which is the major contributor to the factory's energy usage at 38%. In this work, the Energy Performance Indicators (EnPI) of the CAS is predicted using KNN by employing the variables from CAS itself. The collected variables are first analyzed using Dataiku software and correlation matrix and heatmap technique, giving two sets of key features. The predicted EnPI showed high accuracy when compared to the actual values.

articleTitle: Linux Forensic Analysis and Extraction Tool
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Digital forensics is a crucial discipline in the field of cybersecurity, involving the systematic examination of electronic devices to uncover, analyze, and preserve digital evidence for investigative purposes. In this context, Linux, as an operating system, presents unique challenges and opportunities for forensic investigators. Linux forensic analysis requires a deep understanding of its distinctive commands, file systems, and log files, which serve as primary sources for tracing and understanding security incidents. This paper delves into the fundamentals of digital forensics and explores the specific nuances of Linux forensic analysis. We highlight common Linux artifacts that play a pivotal role in investigations, shedding light on their significance. To enhance the efficiency of forensic investigations, we propose the development of an extraction tool. This tool aims to automate the retrieval of Linux artifacts, providing investigators with a streamlined and systematic approach to data collection. By creating a bridge between the intricacies of Linux systems and the needs of forensic investigators, this extraction tool is poised to contribute significantly to the advancement of Linux forensic analysis.

articleTitle: Simplified Artificial Neural Network Configuration in R Programming for Predictive Modelling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: The configuration of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) in the context of predictive modelling can provide considerable difficulty owing to the complex nature of their arrangements and the need for meticulous hyperparameter adjustment. The present study addresses the issue by proposing a more straightforward methodology for configuring Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) through the R programming language. The methodology presented in this study offers a systematic and comprehensive framework, ensuring accessibility and simplicity of implementation. This approach aims to enhance the usability of Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) for practitioners who need advanced machine learning knowledge. In order to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed methodology, a series of experiments were conducted on a case study in sustainable energy research. This study makes a valuable contribution to academic discipline by establishing a connection between artificial neural network (ANN) theory and its practical application. This study aims to enhance the accessibility of artificial neural network (ANN) setup and provide significant insights to further progress predictive modelling, specifically focusing on sustainable energy research.

articleTitle: Driving Alert Application Based On Facial Expression Using Landmark Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)

authors.preferredName: Syed Mohd Zahid Syed Zainal Ariffin

abstract: Many factors contribute to traffic mishaps, the vast majority are the result of human error, such as fatigue. Therefore, this problem prompts the idea to monitor a driver's eyes and detect the sleepy and drowsy state of the driver. A driving alert application based on facial expression recognition is developed to materialize the idea. This application intends to help in decreasing the risks of road accidents by providing an alarm to alert users while driving in a sleepy or drowsy state. The application can determine the state of the drivers in three modes which is normal, sleepy, and drowsy by implementing the BlazeFace framework and landmark algorithm. Accuracy tests were done, and the results produced high accuracy for normal lighting conditions and moderately accurate in low light conditions.

articleTitle: Development of an anodic aluminum oxide membrane for a wearable hemodialysis machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Kidney failure poses a significant global health challenge, necessitating viable treatment options for patients. Two primary methods of survival include kidney transplantation and regular dialysis sessions. However, the latter requires patients to frequently visit hospitals, leading to a substantial disruption in their lifestyle. This paper focuses on the development of an Anodic Aluminum Oxide (AAO) membrane for a wearable hemodialysis machine. The AAO membrane was fabricated through a two-stage anodization process. Prior to anodization, the sample underwent ultrasonic cleaning, annealing, and electro-polishing using a 1:4 ratio solution of perchloric acid and ethanol. Subsequently, the sample was examined using a scanning electron microscope (SEM) to evaluate its structural properties. The SEM analysis revealed that the AAO membrane possessed regular, straight, and controllable pores, ideal for efficient blood filtration. This finding holds promise for the utilization of the AAO membrane in the wearable hemodialysis machine, offering a potential alternative to traditional dialysis methods. By integrating the AAO membrane into the device, patients can experience improved mobility and flexibility, as they are no longer confined to frequent hospital visits. Further research and development in this field could revolutionize the treatment of kidney failure, enhancing the quality of life for patients and providing them with a more convenient and effective solution for blood filtration.

articleTitle: Saie’i Ritual Tracking System Using Geo-Fencing Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Hajj and Umrah are holy events that are performed by millions of Muslim pilgrims all around the world every year. Saie’i is part of a ritual that should be performed by the pilgrims to complete their Hajj and Umrah. Upon performing the Saie'i ritual, a few pilgrims encountered problems. The most common problems are difficulties remembering how many rounds of Saie'i ritual had been performed and the appropriate prayer to recite. As a result of our research, we have decided to support the Saie'i ritual by providing an automatic tracker of the pilgrims while they perform their ritual. A study on location tracking with a global positioning system (GPS) for tracking a real-time location and guided support system has been conducted with the geo-fencing technique. A prototype has been developed and tested in Persiaran Venice 2 Seri Manjung, Perak, simulating the real Saie’i location in Mecca. With the ability to track the user's movement together with smart guidance, this prototype will give great help to the pilgrims and related agencies in handling such an important activity during Umrah and Hajj.

articleTitle: Optimizing Ergonomics in Mobile Device Design: Enhancing User Comfort and Usability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Mobile phones are evolving at a faster pace than ever. Notable instances are on how users hold their smartphones which can also affect the user's comfort. Even with the latest and trendy design innovations, smartphones still encounter challenges due to their physical design. This paper focuses on the investigation on how the ergonomics in a mobile phone's physical design can affect the user's preference. As part of its data gathering procedure, survey questionnaires were handed out to mobile phone users which then reveal their preferences, taking into account factors such as user comfort, usability, and satisfaction in utilizing their preferred mobile device. After analysis of the data gathered, where factors such as one-handed use of smartphones and its thickness were considered, the overall results have shown that the physical parameters of mobile devices are negatively correlated with the ergonomic aspects.

articleTitle: Implementation of Cloud gaming using the Chrome Remote Desktop Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Cloud gaming is an attractive alternative for gamers without having to have expensive hardware. Chrome Remote Desktop method helps to access video games on cloud gaming platforms remotely. This research was carried out by creating a cloud gaming server using Docker and testing cloud gaming on Xbox. Testing was carried out using the Chrome Remote Desktop method and without using this method. The main focus of testing is resource usage (CPU, RAM, and system security). Test results show that using the Chrome Remote Desktop method on the Docker cloud gaming server can increase CPU and RAM usage more efficiently. Meanwhile, cloud gaming testing on Xbox using the CRD method shows higher CPU usage and more efficient RAM. The Chrome Remote Desktop method helps users access video games via cloud gaming. In other words, what will appear on the laptop will also appear on the Android that has been connected.

articleTitle: An Engaging Android App for Arabic-speaking Autistic Kids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Autism spectrum has been noticeably extracted in the last few years. This has led to rising the world awareness about this syndrome. As a result, many institutes were established around the world in order to serve people diagnosed with Autism. In the same context, the high technology sector has shown an interest in this area by presenting a number of smartphone applications (apps) dedicated to help the autistics to merge in their communities and to accomplish daily life tasks efficiently. Motivated by that, this work aims to present MOLHEM as an Android app that comes with an interactive chatbot. The proposed system in general tries to enhance the Arabic autistic children’s different social and academic skills. In addition to that, the system presents a chat system in order to create real life conversations in Arabic or English with the child. Moreover, the parents will be able to control the child’s usage of the app. MOLHEM was tested by a group of possible users for one month and the feedbacks were very positive. Finally, as a part of our futures plans, we aim to add new features like creating an IOS version of the app, adding new languages, and including artificial intelligence techniques.

articleTitle: Classification of Malocclusion using Convolutional Neural Network and Knowledge-Based Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This paper presents a classification of malocclusion using convolutional neural networks (CNN) and knowledge-based systems (KBS). Malocclusion is a dental abnormality and occlusal feature that deviates from the ideal occlusion. Early detection and treatment can resolve the malocclusion problem. However, the process of detection takes time, and there are also cases of misdiagnosis of the malocclusion in referral letters for an orthodontist. Thus, the use of machine learning (ML) algorithms is needed to facilitate the detection and derive a more accurate classification of the malocclusion. The dataset has undergone pre-processing that includes standardising the image size and several processes of augmentation. The dataset used for this research is 1,064 intraoral images of 236 patients. The system was developed using the ResNet-50 model with an accuracy of 61.20%, precision, recall, and F1-score values of 68%, 61%, and 60%, respectively. This research has developed a system that is able to classify malocclusion based on the IOTN that is currently being used by orthodontists. The classification emphasises classifying the five main grades of IOTN, which include grades Very Great, Great, Moderate, Little, and None. In conclusion, all three objectives of this research have been accomplished, and each objective's deliverables are detailed in this research. In the future, a better system for classifying malocclusion based on the IOTN should be developed.

articleTitle: On-chip Self-test Solutions for ADC survey and analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: It is critical for analog-to-digital converter (ADC) systems to obtain quicker and more accurate devices; therefore, ADC testing is critical. As the cost of testing rises, various efficient test techniques with low power, low area occupancy, and error-free converters are required. The main objectives of this research are to summaries the errors, standards, test technologies, and self-healing strategies used in ADC. Furthermore, the difficulties encountered by the typical ADC converter must be solved. These problems, including as speed, complexity, and area, in order to increase ADC functioning. The built-in self-test (BIST) methodology is one method for overcoming these obstacles, and it pushes researchers to find acceptable solutions. After demonstrating the difficulties with the ADC-BIST, it also presents the closely related work carried out or proposed to address existing concerns and constraints. The ADC converter includes a test circuit on an integrated circuit that refers to system-on-chips to reduce cost, noise, and size.

articleTitle: Assessing Web Performance of Malaysian University Website
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: University websites are gaining importance rapidly, making it crucial to ensure its well-designed, user-friendly, and perform optimally. However, there is a lack of research on the web performance of Malaysian university websites, making it challenging for universities to determine the necessary steps to enhance their websites' performance. The research aims to evaluate and enhance the web performance of Malaysian university websites. This study utilized an experimental approach by employing performance metrics from Google Lighthouse version 10.0.1 to measure the web performance of these websites and examine website design and content to identify factors that contributed to poor performance and user experience. The strategies were developed to improve website performance and enhance user experience through Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) and Web Performance Index (WPI). This research will contribute to the existing knowledge on website performance and provide valuable insights and recommendations for enhancing the online presence and reputation of Malaysian universities.

articleTitle: Robust Reversible Image Watermarking based on Independent Embedding Domain and Pixel Value Ordering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Robust reversible watermarking (RRW) schemes play a critical role in vulnerable applications, such as medical imaging, military and remote sensing, which require high fidelity and robustness. Furthermore, an RRW is challenging because it can solve watermark embedding and extraction in lossless and lossy environments. A two-stage RRW approach based on independent embedding domain (IED) has been presented by Wang et al. This paper proposes an RRW scheme through IED with a reversible watermarking method based on pixel value ordering (PVO). In contrast to Wang et al.'s scheme, which relies on threshold-based histogram shifting in reversible phase, our proposed method designs and modifies only the highest and lowest values in a block of pixels. Reversibility is guaranteed as it keeps the PVO of each block unchanged during embedding, thereby reducing distortion in the embedded content. The RRW approach based on IED and PVO results improved imperceptibility over the current state-of-the-art technique.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of HiveQL and SparkSQL Query Performance in a Cluster Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This paper conducts a rigorous comparative analysis of query processing in a cluster environment, employing HiveQL and SparkSQL. Despite their shared SQL-like querying capabilities, their unique architectures and optimizations yield divergent performance outcomes. HiveQL relies on MapReduce, introducing potential bottlenecks for complex queries, whereas SparkSQL leverages in-memory processing, contributing to expedited execution. Consequently, an imperative performance and scalability evaluation is undertaken, with a focus on table schemas and query complexity, providing critical insights for technology selection. The paper introduces a comprehensive performance and scalability analysis framework, furnishing nuanced insights into performance nuances based on table schemas and query intricacies, thereby empowering data professionals in optimal tool selection and design refinement within the dynamic realm of big data environments.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Multivariate and Univariate Time-Series Forecasting for Oil Production
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Production networks and processing facilities can be very complex, with multiple interactions and constraints. It is become a problem whenever the "helicopter view" of the entire production profile, or composite information of the field is required, moreover to see what will happen in the next upcoming time frame. This research presents a study of forecasting techniques for oil production. The goal of the study is to evaluate the performance of different forecasting methods and identify the most effective approaches for predicting future total oil production. The study includes a review of relevant literature, a description of the data and methods used, and an analysis of the results. This study compared two methods for forecasting time-series data: Simple Moving Average (SMA), Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with exogenous variable (SARIMAX), and multivariate time-series forecasting using Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). Multivariate time series forecasting, especially with LightGBM, was found to be highly effective for predicting oil production data. LightGBM showed similar performance to SMA in terms of Mean Absolute Error (MAE) score, with MAE of 3748.71, compared to SMA's MAE of 3853.04. This research also revealed that SARIMAX has the highest MAE value 5280.83. The oilfield total production chart signature, and along with its forecast, seems producing the oil asymptotically since 2021, unless there is any significant intervention, such as discovery of huge oil reserve or on the other hand, a notable fundamental event that accelerate the decline to another low level.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of different electron transport layer for Perovskite Solar Cell with NiO as hole transport layer using SCAPS 1D
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Perovskite solar cells have garnered significant attention from solar cell researchers due to their potential for achieving high efficiency. There is promising avenue for enhancing stability and reducing fabrication costs by substituting the transport layer. Comparative analysis was conducted between two devices featuring distinct structures: TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/NiO and ZnO/CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/NiO. To evaluate the performance of each electron transport layer (ETL), the SCAPS 1D tool was employed. The investigation involved varying the thickness of the absorber, electron transport layer, and hole transport layer, allowing for a comprehensive assessment of key parameters such as voltage at open circuit (Voc), short circuit current density (Jsc), fill factor (FF), and overall efficiency (PCE%). When employing TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as the ETL, the achieved efficiency stands at 24.08%. In contrast, utilizing Zinc Oxide (ZnO) as the ETL yields a slightly higher efficiency of 24.29%. These findings show influence of transport layer materials to overall performance of perovskite solar cells.

articleTitle: Corpus-based Sequence to Sequence with Luong Attention Mechanism for Ilocano to English Translation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Effective communication is a vital means of conveying ideas, yet language barriers often pose significant challenges for individuals and groups conversing in different languages and dialects. These challenges can result in misunderstandings and misinterpretations due to a lack of clarity in expression. Current Ilocano-English translation systems provide some assistance. However, they struggle with translating Ilocano accurately, especially when the input includes sentences with a higher number of words. To address this issue, our study developed a translator using the Seq2Seq model with Luong Attention Mechanism and employs Neural Machine Translation techniques. The developed translator application achieved notable results with an accuracy of 43.95% for English to Ilocano translation and 81.25% accuracy for Ilocano to English translation, along with a BLEU score of 2.50 and 15.42 across all n-gram levels (1-4 words), respectively. These findings contribute to bridging language barriers and enhancing cross-linguistic communication.

articleTitle: Resin-Based Classification of Plastic Bottles Waste using CNN Architectures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: The large use of plastic causes plastic waste problems in the environment. Recycling has become one of the solutions to deal with plastic pollution. Considering plastic waste is required to be separated based on the type of resin in the recycling process, the sorting process becomes more challenging. In this research, we aim to evaluate and compare the accuracy of the classification of plastic bottle waste by plastic resin type based on images using three CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks) architecture models. The CNN architectures used are ResNet50, DenseNet201, and InceptionResNetV2. We focus on PET and HDPE plastic bottles as the target object, and we develop the dataset by collecting about 1000 images for each class. The result shows that with a 99.4% accuracy rate, ResNet50 shows a better performance compared to DenseNet201 and InceptionResNetV2.

articleTitle: Methodology to Prevent Voltage Collapse During On Load Tap Changing Transformer Operation Under Network Contingencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: The operation of On Load Tap Changing Transformer (OLTC) in a normal state can maintain the desired voltage but can also increase the risk of a voltage collapse under certain operating conditions like network contingencies such as outage of a transmission line. Hence, OLTC operation can be both a boon and a curse in voltage control based on the operating condition of the power system. This paper is investigated the effect of the tap changes in the voltage instability process under network contingencies. For this sake, instability may be obtained as a consequence of a network contingency. This paper also discusses the reverse action that the secondary voltage of a transformer is pulled down when the tap position of OLTC is raised to increase the secondary voltage under network contingencies. The performance of the reversal OLTC with the placement of the FACTS device Static VAR Compensator (SVC) at the critical load bus is also investigated. The proposed methodology has been effectively tested on an EHV 24 bus equivalent southern region of an Indian power system network.

articleTitle: Squeezed Light Generation Across Dual Octaves with Single-Mode Multichannel Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: The generation of squeezed light across dual octaves with single-mode multichannel nonlinear waveguides exhibits dynamic behavior. In this study, we examine the impact of coherent state initialization, channel interaction, nonlinearity strength, and inter-channel interaction on the generation of squeezed light over several channels. The findings demonstrate that the process of coherent state initialization and the addition of channel interaction significantly enhance the amount of squeezing, hence emphasizing their critical role in the optimization of squeezed light generation. Additionally, an occurrence of squeezing that is not dependent on nonlinearity is observed within a limited range of parameters. This presents opportunities for generating squeezed light in dual-octave systems with many channels.

articleTitle: UiTMBusTracker Mobile Application of Bus Transportation Tracker for UiTM Students
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This research focuses on developing a specialized mobile application tailored for Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) students, aiming to enhance their bus transportation experience. Leveraging contemporary mobile technology and GPS tracking, the application will provide real-time information on bus locations, arrivals, and routes, addressing common commuting challenges. By optimizing student mobility and campus accessibility, the project aims to streamline transportation, reduce congestion, and contribute to a more sustainable campus environment. The application's user-friendly interface and data-driven features align with UiTM's commitment to technological advancement for student welfare, offering a comprehensive solution to improve transportation efficiency and convenience within the campus community. By using the method of Mobile Software Development Life Cycle, the mobile application has been produced to solve the problem that has been stated in this paper.

articleTitle: EcoCharge: Innovative Solar and Wind Charging Station Enabled by Solid Waste Contributions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This research introduces a waste disposal solution that harnesses the power of microcontroller-controlled charging stations fueled by renewable solar and wind energy sources. These stations are equipped with sensors to detect incoming waste inputs, offering an intuitive interface that displays the available charging time for each chamber. Users can easily allocate the available time to the charge timer using designated buttons, allowing for efficient charging in the respective relay slots. An analysis of the system revealed critical insights. Peak battery charging performance was identified between 11:00 am to 1:00 pm, independent of the load presence, underscoring the efficiency of the proposed technology. Furthermore, the hourly battery percentage discharge in the absence of any power source was acceptable. This innovative approach not only addresses waste disposal challenges but also promotes sustainability through renewable energy utilization, making it a promising solution for a cleaner and more efficient waste management system.

articleTitle: A Log Aggregation Design Criteria for Robust SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) in Enhancing Threat Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Security Operations Centers (SOCs) play a vital role in protecting organizations from cyber threats. Supported by skilled Security Analysts, they are the first line of defense, monitoring and responding to incidents. The Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system is a critical tool for managing log data efficiently. This research focuses on optimizing log data aggregation within a SOC's SIEM framework. By exploring various log aggregation techniques, we aim to enhance the performance of data collectors, leading to quicker response times and improved security. This research contributes to a more robust defense against the ever-changing landscape of cyber threats. It empowers organizations to face evolving challenges with confidence and resilience.

Author Keywords: Security Information and Event Management System (SIEM)

articleTitle: Mixed Operation in Overlay Networks: Performance Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Secondary sources (SSs) assist primary sources (PSs) as a prize for accessing primary frequency bands for communication in overlay networks, significantly ameliorating spectral efficiency. To further meliorate spectral efficiency, energy efficiency, and system performance, this paper proposes a mixed operation in which SSs switch cleverly between direct communication and relaying communication. The performance of the mixed operation in overlay networks is assessed extensively and thoroughly in innumerable real-world scenarios to prove the effectiveness of the proposed operation.

articleTitle: Effects of Imperfect Hardware and Energy Harvesting Nonlinearity on Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: By scavenging radio frequency energy and generating artificial interference, the work aims to meliorate energy efficiency and data security for wireless networks. The security performance is evaluated to study effects of energy harvesting nonlinearity and imperfect hardware on wireless networks with energy scavenging and artificial interference generation. Towards this end, the work presents abundant results generated by MonteCarlo simulations in divergent pivotal specifications. Multiple results expose detrimental impacts of imperfect hardware and energy harvesting nonlinearity but considerable security improvement of scavenging radio frequency energy and generating artificial interference.

articleTitle: BISINDO Hand-Sign Detection Using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a BISINDO hand sign language recognition system using transfer learning methods. The system aims to address the communication challenges faced by the deaf community in interacting with the majority of people and alleviate the feelings of isolation experienced by the deaf and mute society. Two models, SSD MobileNet v2 FPNLite 320x320 and SSD MobileNet v2 FPNLite 640x640, were trained for 20,000 steps using a custom dataset of BISINDO alphabets (A-Z). The results demonstrate the successful detection and recognition of BISINDO alphabet characters by both models. The second model, trained with SSD MobileNet v2 FPNLite 640x640 pre-trained model, exhibited slightly higher accuracy with improved mAP and AR scores. These findings highlight the potential of computer vision technology to facilitate real-time detection and recognition of BISINDO hand signs, enabling effective communication between deaf and hearing individuals. Future research can focus on refining the models, expanding the dataset, and incorporating more comprehensive sign gestures to enhance the system’s accuracy and usability. This research contributes to advancing assistive technologies for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community, fostering inclusivity and accessibility in society.

articleTitle: Prediction of Powerplant Performance by Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: The IEEE Standard 762-1987 introduced a comprehensive set of 25 indices for reporting power plant reliability, availability, and productivity. The sheer number of indices can be impractical, and an univariate indicator is preferable for real-world applications. Developing a single indicator derived from the 25 indices is the work's main theme. This study addresses this issue using machine learning to consolidate these indices, ultimately classifying power plant performance into "performed" and "unperformed." Monthly performance data from 2020 were collected from 570 power plants in the Java-Sumatra interconnected electric system. These data were obtained from the Generation Availability Information System, a proprietary application owned by the Indonesia National Electric Power Company. Using the $k$-means clustering method, we classified the performance of these power plants. The clustering process was supplemented with the opinions of seven experts with extensive experience in the system. The comparison between machine learning classifications and expert opinions is presented.

articleTitle: Linear and Nonlinear Predictive Models for Manila City’s Condition and People Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Manila is the capital city of the Philippines. According to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), Manila is one of the most populated cities in the country, and it is continuously growing. Therefore, the capability to provide homes or spaces for both Filipino and foreign residents is difficult and gets more difficult over time. Thus, prediction and evaluation of the condition and people satisfaction (C&PS) in Manila are very significant and needed. The authors identified 30 C&PS factors. The structural equation modeling (SEM) and artificial neural network (ANN) were used for linear and nonlinear prediction assessment of these factors, respectively. Moreover, the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and sensitivity analysis (SA) were used for the evaluation of variables. The results of the synthesis methods, SEM-AHP and ANN-SA, would provide an informative vision for the PSA.

articleTitle: Found It! Object Tracker Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Losing items is a frequent problem that many people deal with on a daily basis. It can cause annoyance, wasted time, and perhaps even financial loss. The stress and difficulty of trying to find lost items, whether they be phones, keys, or other valuables, can interfere with our daily routines and cause needlessly high levels of anxiety. This challenge may be especially difficult for those who struggle to keep track of their belongings due to cognitive impairments or disabilities. Thus, this project is used to help people to find their missing item by attaching the item with the Found It! Object Tracker Tag. The mobile application can be used to track the misplaced item by showing the distance of the tag and mobile phone. The application can share the tag location to family members and friends through Telegram. This application also has crowd finding features where the user can view people lost tag and they also can share their lost tag location. They will need to share their number phone and message for people to contact when they find it. In this research study, the System Usability Scale (SUS), a methodology that comprises of 10 questions about the program's usefulness, will be utilized to evaluate the usability of the Found It! Mobile App for Object Tracking.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Xception Networks and Short-Time Fourier Transform Spectrograms for Motor Imagery Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This study seeks to explore the success of the Xception convolutional neural network and short-time Fourier transform in classifying EEG signals with limited training samples using pre-trained deep transfer learning. So far, most deep learning research has concentrated on one-dimensional time series inputs. Two-dimensional inputs are another excellent way of giving EEG signals to deep learning. This study used a two-dimensional STFT-based method to transform EEG signals into images and Xception for classification. BCI Competition IV dataset 2b, which includes nine participants, was used to evaluate the performance. This study is the first to report the STFT + Xception approach results for classifying motor imagery signals. It achieved good results from a small number of MIEEG data, averaging over 80% for nine subjects with a very low standard deviation of 2.9% between subjects. Applying data augmentation and training from scratch with more data can show more successful results in the future.

articleTitle: An Improved Archimedes Optimization Algorithm for Solving Optimization Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: The Archimedes Optimization Algorithm (AOA) algorithm, a multi-agent-based metaheuristic, has garnered attention for its remarkable accuracy in real-world optimization. This research addresses solutions for the inherent limitation of original AOA, notably its susceptibility to uneven exploration and exploitation phases and its propensity to become ensnared in local optima. To overcome these limitations, we employ two strategies: the modification of the density decreasing factor and the introduction of a safe updating mechanism inspired by game theory. These enhancements are subjected to rigorous evaluation using 23 benchmark functions, and their performance is compared against that of the original AOA and other prominent algorithms, including the Multiverse Optimization (MVO), Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm (GOA), Sine Cosine Algorithm (SCA), and Ant Lion Optimizer (ALO). The test results reveal significant improvements achieved by the newly proposed improved AOA (IAOA), surpassing the performance of the original AOA in 69% of the optimization cases among the 23 test functions. It is noteworthy that it also outperformed the other mentioned algorithms. The potential of the proposed algorithm as an effective tool for addressing real-world optimization challenges is underscored by these encouraging findings, adhering to research conventions.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Edge Caching for Video Streaming in 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: The advent of 5G networks has brought significant advancements in the Quality of Service (QoS) provided to various applications, including video streaming. However, the increasing demand for high-quality video streaming, coupled with the need for low latency and improved user experience, poses challenges for the existing network architecture. Recently, there have been several proposals to utilize machine learning techniques in order to improve the QoS for mobile video users. These techniques aim to enhance various aspects of video delivery, such as video streaming, video compression, and video adaptation. This paper aims to explore the use of edge caching machine learning-based technique for video streaming services. In this paper, proof-of-concept experiments and the setup of a Hybrid Cloud-Edge Architecture with Amazon Web Services are presented. The experimental results demonstrate that applying machine learning to cloud-edge caching architecture is both feasible and effective.

articleTitle: Secure Mobile Login using Three-Layer Graphical User Interface (GUI) Authentication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Mobile devices are very important in our daily life nowadays. However, it has security drawbacks particularly in device authentication. Conventional text-based passwords are exposed to vulnerabilities. Simple passwords are susceptible to brute-force attacks, while complex ones are difficult to recall, leading to forgetfulness and user frustration. This research proposes an integration of a Graphical User Interface (GUI) authentication system within mobile applications which are recognition-based, recall-based, and cued-recall authentication. The mobile application is developed using Flutter which is a practical exemplar of the three-tier GUI authentication system. A questionnaire was distributed among twenty (20) users which focuses on usability, design scheme and security level of the mobile application. The result findings indicate the significance of the three-layer GUI authentication presenting a holistic approach of mobile security while preserving user convenience. The implication of this research promotes a more secure digital landscape, which redefine mobile security authentication practices for the better.

articleTitle: Rule-based Self-supervised learning Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring system for residential houses
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Real-time non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) systems have gained significant importance in various applications, including demand-side management, appliance anomaly detection, and ambient assisted living. While numerous research-based solutions have been developed over the past two decades, still it remains a need for an affordable application-level NILM solution. In this paper, we present a novel rule-based self-supervised approach that operates within a low-price range. Our proposed methodology offers automatic identification of unknown appliances within the system, achieving real-time appliance identification with a satisfactory level of accuracy. We contribute to the development of a cost-effective and efficient solution for non-intrusive load monitoring, enabling applications across diverse domains.

articleTitle: Lighting up Adorsho Char: A solar PV Based Energy Harvesting System for a Remote Island of Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Solar energy is a promising and environmentally sustainable energy option that offers a feasible and economically efficient solution for providing electricity to off-grid and remote places in Bangladesh. This study aims to comprehensively examine the viability of deploying and utilising solar energy on Adorsho Chor, a remote island located adjacent to the Feni River in Bangladesh. The study utilises a simulation-based methodology, including the software tools PVSOL and PVsyst, to obtain meteorological data, simulate solar panels, and estimate the energy yield. In this study, the LG330N1C-A5 solar PV module was selected, together with the SUN2000 12 KTL M2 inverter and the LUNA2000-5KW-E0 battery, both manufactured by Huawei Technologies, to ensure the integration and efficiency of the system design. In our investigation, a total of 240 solar modules were employed to simulate and assess energy yield. The evaluation conducted in this study consisted of four separate panel orientations, which comprised both mono-facial and bifacial configurations. The research conducted encompassed a comparative examination of several configurations, evaluating significant metrics like annual photovoltaic (PV) energy output, specific production, and performance ratios. According to the findings of the study, the maximum annual photovoltaic (PV) energy output recorded was 129,607.9 kilowatt-hours (kWh). This noteworthy result was obtained for bifacial panels under specific parameters, namely a tilt angle of 25 degrees and an azimuth of 180 degrees, which led to a favourable specific production value of 1,631 kWh per kilowatt-peak (kWp). Furthermore, a thorough examination of the monthly energy variation for each orientation was undertaken in order to aid in making well-informed choices regarding sustainable energy solutions in this isolated area.

articleTitle: Sensorimotor Activity Patterns using Machine Learning: Assessing the Impact of Auditory Timing Perception and Comparing Different Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Perception and action are the characteristics of the human condition and define our impact on the world around us. The brain's ability to effectively sort and incorporate these signals for flawless interactions with the environment gives rise to the hypothesis that these processes share an integrated set of representations, including our arbitrary sense of time. Interesting studies investigate how simultaneous activities affect our ability to keep track of time when we consciously move from one place to another. Surprisingly, no study has yet delved into the possibility of predicting simultaneous movements based on our time estimates or vice-versa. The purpose of this study is to examine the role of machine learning in the statistical prediction of sensorimotor tasks explicitly involving isolated auditory tones and arm motions, or both simultaneously based on conscious timed actions. The dataset was collected via Kaggle and consisted of 210 trials across 20 right-handed participants with each participant completing 14 trials in a block, for a total of 96 trials, and the sequence of the conditions was pseudo-randomized. Using data from seven distinct features representing a variety of consciously timed activities, nine ML regressor-type models have been trained to produce a statistical prediction of sensorimotor tasks. Each of the nine regressor models has its hyperparameters optimized using RandomizedSearchCV for better performance. The various performance matrices of ML algorithms were compared, including the MAE, RMSE, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, MARE, NSE, and residual plots.

articleTitle: Performance of Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks in Heterogeneous Traffic Load Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: A Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) consists of small, low-cost, and resource-constrained sensor nodes that collect environmental data and communicate wirelessly to deliver data to the sink node. Integration of WSN and Internet of Things (IoTs) becomes a crucial design parameter due to the limited coverage provided by WiFi within about 10m range from an access point for internet connectivity. WSN extends the coverage over 100 meters using multi-hop communication with reliable connections. The self-configure feature to establish a WSN allows the deployment of a large number of IoT devices. In a typical IoT application, the IoT devices generate data at different rates, leading to a heterogeneous traffic load. The objective of this paper is to determine the behavior of Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks (RPL) in the heterogeneous traffic load of WSN. Cooja is used as the simulation tool. RPL is simulated in a random topology network consisting of 50 sensor nodes and one sink. The sensor nodes are divided into four groups and each group generates a different traffic load to demonstrate heterogeneous WSN. Two simulation scenarios are considered in this study. The first scenario is a study on RPL performance in different number of node distributions. The second scenario is a study on RPL performance in four different sink positions. The findings show that RPL does not perform the best result when the sink is located at the center of the network. In the heterogeneous traffic load of WSN, RPL provides better performance when the sink is moved slightly closer to the area where the most traffic is generated in the heterogeneous network. The worst RPL performance is observed when the sink position is at the edge of the network. It is also found that RPL performance in heterogeneous traffic load is affected by the overall number of hops to the sink. The smaller number of hops gives a better performance of RPL when compared to the higher number of hops away from the sink.

articleTitle: Influence of YouTube as Coding Language Learning For Academic Achievement
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This study of the research looks at how utilizing YouTube to learn coding languages affects students' academic performance. According to the survey, YouTube can be useful for learning coding languages, especially for individuals who know best visually and audibly. Students who might have difficulty with conventional learning approaches have found YouTube helpful. However, YouTube videos vary greatly, so students must be picky when choosing the best ones. The data was collected in July 2023 with 81 respondents. Data was collected using purposive sampling and all respondents are from Jabodetabek area in Indonesia. It use Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) with SMART PLS as a statistical tool. According to the research, YouTube might be useful for learning coding languages and boosting academic performance. Nevertheless, students should use it as one tool among many and look for top-notch content.

articleTitle: Water Quality Classification Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: Water quality is crucial as it directly affects the ecosystem and human health. However, current water quality classification methods are inefficient because they do not compare prediction accuracy between machine learning methods. In this regard, the objective of this study is to classify water quality based on the proposed machine learning tools. To fulfill that, a preliminary study was conducted by collecting related information in the research domain through articles, electronic books, and online databases. The data collection for the prototype’s dataset was obtained from an electronic book published by the Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources 2021. Subsequently, the data pre-processing phase was conducted by using WEKA software which includes the crucial steps to transform the data into a cleaner format and make the model more accurate. The model for each technique was developed using Python in Jupyter Notebook. The results of the accuracy score for each model were also conducted in this phase. The findings of this research show that the Decision Tree model performs excellently with an accuracy of 97.37% compared to the Support Vector Machine and K-Nearest Neighbour models, with an accuracy of 95.69% and 74.72%, respectively. Consequently, implementing a multi-class classification system can help future researchers classify more accurately and reduce the misclassification of water quality.

articleTitle: Enhanced Barangay Information Management System with Residency Certificate Issuance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This study focuses on developing and evaluating a barangay management information system with a residency certificate issuance feature. Using a development research approach, the system was crafted to meet the specific needs of local communities. The system was evaluated using the Usefulness, Satisfaction, Ease of Use (USE) questionnaire by IT practitioners, IT government employees, and barangay officials The resulting user acceptance and effectiveness ratings showcased a remarkable average score of 4.58. This consensus reflects a strong agreement among participants, underscoring the system's exceptional user-friendly characteristics and innate convenience. Beyond its user-centric design, this system yields substantial advantages for barangays in the realm of local e-governance. By optimizing administrative processes and simplifying document processing, it enhances operational efficiency within the context of digital governance initiatives. Furthermore, its pivotal role in establishing a comprehensive repository of essential records magnifies its potential to reshape local governance in the digital age.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effectiveness of Video-Based Learning in Trading Cryptocurrency, Foreign Exchange and Stock Market
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: In recent years, video-based learning has gained popularity as a potential solution to the challenges of traditional classroom instruction. This literature review delves into the effectiveness of video-based learning in comparative research. It highlights that video-based learning proves to be an effective method for enhancing student engagement and motivation and improving learning outcomes. The data for this review were collected in August 2023, with 132 responses from Indonesians (from the Jabodetabek area) who learned to trade foreign exchange, cryptocurrency, and stock markets as respondents obtained through purposive sampling. After stringent data screening, 109 responses meeting the study's requirements remained, ensuring data integrity by excluding outliers like journals and news articles. It used structural equation modeling (SEM) and SMART PLS as statistical methods and tools. Furthermore, this study emphasizes the importance of addressing potential limitations in the implementation of video-based learning, such as the risk of cognitive overload and the need for adequate technical infrastructure and support. Future research is essential to pinpoint the optimal design and strategies for video-based instruction and to determine its effectiveness in diverse contexts and with varying learner characteristics.

articleTitle: Order Picking System Simulation Model Considering Picking Method and Picker Route to Improve Warehouse Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study to improve warehouse performance by optimizing the order-picking process. The authors developed a simulation model to analyze the impact of various order-picking methods and tour routes on the order-picking time. The study reveals that the current order-picking system is plagued with high unfinished picklists and prolonged waiting times, negatively impacting warehouse performance. To address these issues, the authors propose 12 improvement scenarios that combine different tour routes, picking methods, and picker numbers. The findings suggest that transitioning to a pick-by-voice picking method is more effective in reducing incomplete picklists than increasing the number of pickers. The most efficient scenario is Scenario 8, which incorporates the mid-point route, pick-by-voice picking method, and two pickers. The paper concludes that the choice of the order-picking method significantly influences warehouse performance, thereby encouraging future research to explore other order-picking methods and delve deeper into the process.

articleTitle: Comparison of Various Colorization Techniques for MRI Brain Tumor Segmentation using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Recent Advances and Innovations in Engineering (ICRAIE)
abstract: In the realm of image processing and computer vision, image segmentation takes on a foundational role, serving as a critical inception task for diverse analyses, especially in the application of brain tumor detection. Given the grayscale nature of MRI brain tumor images, the primary objective of this study was to explore the effects of employing various colorization techniques on the accuracy of MRI brain tumor segmentation.
